A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PASs-MoE study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A.1–A.3 are readable and can be matched across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original MLLM-CTBench experiments, including baseline comparisons, component ablations, routing analyses, and appendix experiments on reversed task order and random regularization.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds reported L2P comparisons and a sensitivity experiment for LoRA-B stabilization.

M1.justification: Section 4.3 extends the specified PASs-RS objective from stabilizing A rows to separately stabilizing A rows and paired B columns, using the same importance weights. This is a limited extension of the existing stabilization component; PASs-based routing and importance estimation remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same seven MLLM-CTBench tasks, source datasets, modalities, and forward/reverse task streams. Appendix Tables 4–5 retain the dataset coverage and task requirements; Table 6's reversed column order does not introduce another scenario.

E2.justification: L2P gains result rows in both the main comparison, Table 1, and the reverse-order comparison, Table 6. v1 mentioned L2P but provided no corresponding results. Other comparator rows are retained, including HiDe-LLaVA under standardized capitalization.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 corrects the written forgetting formula from post-task minus final accuracy to final minus post-task accuracy. The stated regularization configuration changes from a single coefficient of 5e-4 to λA=5e-4 and λB=5e-5, and the new B sweep fixes λA while varying λB. Data splits and training budgets remain unchanged; these reported revisions do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Section 5.3.2 and new Figure 5 add a targeted sensitivity study of B stabilization with A stabilization fixed. Existing component and expert-count ablations, routing and rank analyses, training curves, and appendix task-order and random-regularization experiments are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify random seed 42 and retain median/interquartile-range summaries across rank-importance bins. No repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: New L2P results report AP/BWT of 31.65/-14.97 in Table 1 and 28.96/-15.49 in Table 6. Figure 5 adds B-sensitivity results, with AP peaking at λB=2.5e-4. Matched existing table entries remain unchanged, including PASs-MoE AP of 48.46 and 46.67 for the two task orders; Figure 4 also retains its values.

T1.justification: Equation 11 adds a mathematical definition of the B-column stabilization penalty and revises the combined objective. Section 5.1 also reverses the signed forgetting definition. The PASs definition and remaining mathematical development are retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: PASs addresses misaligned co-drift through capability-aligned routing and rank stabilization at fixed capacity, improving performance and retention. The headline AP advantage remains unchanged.

C2.justification: Sections 4.3 and 5.3.2 newly distinguish A as the structural anchor from B stabilization as complementary and more sensitive to tuning. Excessive B regularization is interpreted as restricting plasticity. Existing interpretations of routing drift and rank importance, and the substantive limitations, remain largely unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a promise to release code upon acceptance with a statement of public availability and a repository URL. v2 also specifies separate A/B coefficients and explicitly describes paired A/B directions in Appendix A.3. The repository's actual contents or accessibility cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds recent references on multimodal representations, MoE, and PEFT, including a short connection to compact reasoning embeddings, and removes Chaudhry et al. (2020). The central positioning of PASs as parameter-induced rather than statistics-derived remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized passages expand the related work, stabilization explanation, metric convention, and sensitivity discussion. v2 adds corresponding-author markers and acknowledgments and removes the unsupported sentence promising zero-shot and multitask result bounds. The overall section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 5, redraws Figure 4 with revised axis spacing and λA labeling, and relocates or renumbers retained displays. Tables 1 and 6 gain L2P rows; Table 6 reverses its task columns and clarifies that they follow training order. The basic document layout remains consistent.

improvement.justification: The corrected forgetting definition resolves an inconsistency with the reported signs, while L2P results and the B-sensitivity analysis improve empirical completeness. Explicit A/B regularization details and the stated code location also improve reproducibility information. These are limited gains: coverage and headline results remain unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish whether retained scores were rerun under the expanded objective.
